title: KELT-9b — a planet in stellar heat

segments.en: This gas giant's dayside is hotter than the surfaces of some stars.
segments.en_cap: This gas giant's dayside | is hotter than | the surfaces of | some stars.

segments.en: Spitzer's infrared data put its dayside near forty-six hundred kelvin.
segments.en_cap: Spitzer's infrared data | put its dayside near | 4,600 kelvin.

segments.en: Even the night glows at roughly twenty-six hundred kelvin, despite facing away.
segments.en_cap: Even the night glows at | roughly 2,600 kelvin, | despite facing away.

segments.en: Models suggest heat splits hydrogen molecules into atoms, absorbing energy. Gas carries them toward the cooler night.
segments.en_cap: Models suggest heat | splits hydrogen molecules | into atoms, | absorbing energy. | Gas carries them toward | the cooler night.

segments.en: There, atoms can join back into molecules, releasing energy. That helps move heat around the planet, through chemical changes.
segments.en_cap: There, atoms can join | back into molecules, | releasing energy. | That helps move heat | around the planet, | through chemical changes.

segments.en: Its whole year lasts about thirty-six hours, on an orbit almost over its star's poles.
segments.en_cap: Its whole year lasts | about 36 hours, | on an orbit almost over | its star's poles.

segments.en: A gas giant, almost twice Jupiter's radius.
segments.en_cap: A gas giant, | almost twice | Jupiter's radius.

segments.en: There is no solid surface to stand on, even on the nightside.
segments.en_cap: There is no solid surface | to stand on, | even on the nightside.

segments.en: A planet, with a dayside hotter than some stellar surfaces.
